text:
# Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH)

MIDH is a centrally sponsored horticulture-development scheme covering fruits, vegetables and other horticultural crops. Protected cultivation is one of the areas covered through operational guidelines and component-based assistance.

The 2025 MIDH/NHB guidelines include protected-cultivation cost norms and assistance patterns, including components related to polyhouses, cultivation of high-value crops, mulching and certain add-on technologies. Exact admissible cost, beneficiary area, state implementation and assistance can change through notifications.

source_name: Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture
text:
## Namma Krushi chatbot response pattern

When a farmer asks “Can I get subsidy for a polyhouse?”, answer that protected cultivation is supported under MIDH/NHB frameworks, then provide the official MIDH/NHB link and instruct the farmer to verify the current Karnataka implementation, eligible structure, area limit, category and application window with the Karnataka Horticulture Department.

Do not hard-code a single subsidy percentage as universally applicable. The applicable pattern depends on the component and current guidelines.

# PM-KISAN

PM-KISAN is a Central Sector scheme funded by the Government of India. The official portal states that eligible landholding farmer families receive income support of ₹6,000 per year in three equal instalments, subject to scheme eligibility and exclusion categories.

The state/UT identifies eligible farmer families and funds are transferred directly to beneficiary bank accounts. Exclusion categories apply to several higher-income or specified institutional/professional categories.

For eligibility checks, registration status or corrections, the chatbot should send the farmer to the official PM-KISAN portal because records and requirements are personal and time-sensitive.

# Kisan Credit Card (KCC)

KCC is designed to provide farmers timely credit for cultivation and related needs through a simplified credit framework. The myScheme page lists short-term crop requirements, post-harvest expenses, produce marketing, certain household consumption needs, maintenance of farm assets and investment credit for agriculture/allied activities within the scheme framework.

Eligibility includes owner-cultivators and can include tenant farmers, oral lessees, sharecroppers and eligible farmer groups subject to bank rules. The exact credit limit and documentation are determined by the lending institution and local scale of finance.

The chatbot should provide the official myScheme/bank route and avoid promising approval or a fixed loan amount.

# Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)

PMFBY is the national crop-insurance program administered by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare. The official portal provides farmer enrollment, premium calculation, application status, policy-related tools, guidelines and loss/grievance support.

Whether tomato or another horticultural crop is insurable depends on notified crops, area and season. The farmer should check the current state/season notification rather than assuming every crop is automatically covered.

Important Karnataka note: the PMFBY portal currently states that direct online enrollment on the national portal is not available for Karnataka and Gujarat because those states enroll farmers through their own portals. The chatbot should therefore direct Karnataka farmers to the appropriate state route and official PMFBY information.

# Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF)

AIF is a Central Sector financing facility intended to support viable post-harvest management infrastructure and community farming assets. Eligible entities include categories such as farmer groups, FPOs, cooperatives, agriculture entrepreneurs and other entities described in current guidelines.

The scheme is more relevant to infrastructure investment than to routine daily crop inputs. A tomato farmer or group may find it relevant for qualifying post-harvest or community assets, aggregation, storage or other eligible infrastructure projects.

The chatbot should not assume a greenhouse itself qualifies under AIF without checking current eligible-project definitions. For protected-cultivation subsidy questions, MIDH/NHB and the state horticulture department are usually the first sources to check.

topic: Karnataka Agriculture and Horticulture Scheme Discovery
text:
# Karnataka scheme discovery

For Karnataka farmers, use official state portals alongside national schemes. Raita Mitra and the Karnataka Department of Horticulture publish agriculture/horticulture services, schemes and department information. myScheme is a national discovery platform that can filter schemes based on eligibility information.

topic: Karnataka Agriculture and Horticulture Scheme Discovery
text:
## Chatbot behavior

If a farmer asks a broad question such as “Which government scheme can help me build a polyhouse?”, first identify the need (protected structure, irrigation, crop insurance, credit, post-harvest infrastructure). Then return the most relevant official scheme category and link.

If the user asks “Am I eligible?”, do not guess from incomplete information. Ask only the minimum relevant factors and still advise checking the current official notification/application portal.

Scheme content should be re-verified periodically because benefit patterns, application windows and implementing departments change.
